summary: CANCELLED handling claims work, resolves stealth ownership before external classification, gives pending move precedence, and otherwise performs the configured cancel/follow-up lifecycle under the resolved root.
cancel_order reads client_order_id, tracks cancellation work, and forwards it as an element of REST cancel_orders(order_ids=...). The identifier contract remains a separately recorded hazard.
place_order generates a client_order_id, normalizes limit price and size, performs a tracked REST create_order, classifies the response fail-closed, and emits an explicit success/error response.

Order/status/log mutations update shared engine_state under state_lock and schedule state_update broadcasts; ticker and spread use separate messages; stealth snapshots periodically serialize manager memory. OrderEngine status samples RuntimeController coherently at its publication boundary, but normal shutdown stores DRAINING/false and later STOPPED is available through admin_status rather than republished engine status. Current browser and terminal consumers map every running=false sample, including STARTING and PAUSED, to a Stopped label.
The dashboard listens on ws://localhost:8765; a client receives products_list then state_update, and subsequent inbound JSON is dispatched by message type.

One drain owner transitions to DRAINING and invokes hooks in order. The early OrderEngine hook blocks incomplete startup but preserves fully launched fill/event workers while the stealth producer stops; full engine cleanup then sets their stop event. The owner waits for tracked work and DRAINING-time hooks until one shared deadline, atomically closes registration, and marks logical STOPPED. Concurrent callers reuse the terminal result; bounded joins or timeout may leave cooperative daemon work exiting afterward.

The unified order-progress path converts cumulative WebSocket state to a delta, appends derived fill/audit data, persists partial-fill progress, publishes event state, and only then allows fill/cancel follow-up routing.

FILLED handling claims follow-up work, resolves root/stealth ownership, updates stealth execution, validates economics and capacity, and creates/registers the resulting follow-up under the flat chain root.
Every 30 seconds OrderEngine rebuilds parent/child maps from database queries and atomically replaces both compatibility dictionaries when its equivalence comparison detects change.

During STARTING the first pause request latches without changing state, complete_startup publishes PAUSED, and resume cannot open admission early. From RUNNING, pause changes state to PAUSED immediately; configured dashboard origins and scheduler exchange actions remain blocked while cancellations, fills, queries, and admin controls continue. Actual transitions into RUNNING notify named admission-open hooks outside controller locks; the stealth bridge uses that edge to publish scheduler work only. Resume returns only PAUSED to RUNNING.
PeriodicReconciler waits its interval and repeats startup reconciliation with configured auto-heal/fill-audit policy until stopped.

Process startup remains non-admitting in STARTING while an early engine-quiesce hook, component hooks, and lock-free signal intent handling are installed before passive stealth hydration and dashboard exposure. Reconciliation completes or is explicitly bypassed, strict schedules activate, periodic registration/start is atomic, and one-shot OrderEngine worker launch plus the initial fee-refresh attempt return. The run_forever callback is the sole readiness publication to RUNNING or latched PAUSED; stop checkpoints prevent later worker publication or readiness revival.

Importing configuration creates the REST wrapper, attempts live product metadata and futures-position reads with cached/empty fallback, constructs the v2 OrderBook behind a compatibility shim, and instantiates global ORDERBOOK.

OrderEngine claims one startup attempt, performs DB hydration and the synchronous initial fee-refresh attempt outside its lifecycle lock with stop checkpoints, and serializes only bounded worker/readiness publication against sticky stop. A partial launch calls retryable cooperative cleanup and never publishes readiness. Completion proves required non-fail-soft Thread.start calls and the fee attempt returned, not optional worker or fee success, complete hydration, worker health, websocket connection/subscription, or a first snapshot.

Startup reconciliation compares REST-open client_order_ids with nonterminal order_parent rows, classifies drift buckets, and auto-heals only exchange-closed/local-open rows; unknown-to-local and exchange-open/local-terminal remain operator review.

Bridge start strictly hydrates persisted stealth rows and starts only the 30-second reconciliation thread. After startup exchange/local reconciliation, or the explicit DISABLE_RECONCILER bypass, activate_decisions builds all derived schedules, starts the sole decision worker, then registers admission-open reconstruction; incomplete hydration, scheduling, worker activation, or hook registration fails closed. The 100ms cadence remains for active compatibility, admission, and overdue deadline/anchor retry rebuilding, but a non-admitting TRIGGERED row has no recurring admission retry.

The deadline worker marks individual anchor schedules due without exchange or database work. The first eligible live ticker claims only the due client_order_ids, invokes the canonical manager path, and rebuilds each deadline. Hidden local-price updates operate normally; the separate revealed-exposure hazard records why canonical fully revealed live placements currently skip cancel-replace.
Condition evaluation selects price threshold, cumulative volume, time delay, spread, product ratio, or composite evaluators through get_evaluator; unknown condition types fall back to time delay.

The bridge reserves each root or follow-up client_order_id and holds its per-order action lock through the complete manager transaction. Canonical creation validates price, size and profitability, persists fail-closed ERROR then parent and active HIDDEN state, publishes cache/lifecycle/schedule state, and completes follow-up audit finalization before the lock is released.

Ordered product ticker events evaluate market/stable-time conditions through the per-order path; TIME_DELAY, ADMISSION_RETRY, and COMPATIBILITY_RECHECK deadline wakes use that same path. CONDITION_HOLD wakes await the next ordered market snapshot, while ANCHOR_REPRICE wakes publish the separate live-ticker handoff. Every condition PENDING/TRIGGERED transition must persist through one fail-closed boundary before lifecycle publication or reveal. Reveal placement uses atomic admission plus inflight registration, is deferred without recurring retry while pause owns admission, and retains snapshot-committed TRIGGERED state without condition re-evaluation. Admission-open publishes one immediate retry; generation fencing leaves one normal 100ms successor owner while active.

Manual stealth move builds an eligibility/price plan, claims MOVE against REPRICE, cancels the active exchange order, pre-inserts a flat-root replacement row, places/classifies it, updates active pointers, and persists move audit.

Every 30 seconds the bridge queries active stealth IDs and loads only IDs missing from manager memory through the canonical lazy-load path, which publishes their derived schedules; it neither refreshes changed cached rows nor evicts cached rows absent/terminal in DB.

Reveal calculates a strategy slice, builds and profitability-checks an execution plan, runs placement hooks, normalizes the exact submission price, pre-inserts/updates placement audit rows, performs post-only retries on safer ticks, classifies response, and finalizes accepted or failed lifecycle state.

The ticker worker publishes each admitted Coinbase snapshot to the stealth scheduler before other local handling. Accepted snapshots update current-state cache, dashboard, persistence, metrics, fee signals, and due anchor work; timestamp-stale snapshots enter the same FIFO as invalidation-only evidence and are suppressed from those downstream consumers.

For an unseen client_order_id, process_user_order creates an order_parent self-root before partial-fill-progress FK writes, tags it externally_created in memory, and allows later local mappings (including stealth placement lookup) to relate it.

The sole private connection retains channel, generation, connection-global sequence, timestamp, and all events through one bounded ordered reducer queue. Subscription acknowledgements, heartbeat, user, and futures messages share one generation watermark; the reducer drops stale/desynchronized work, isolates positions, and collects complete post-bootstrap PATCH/UPDATE rows for whole-envelope canonical dispatch.

Initial snapshot plus PATCH/UPDATE continuation pages accumulate by client_order_id until the first page below 50. Missing initial data and unterminated pagination each time out. Completion performs one drift check and one minimal in-memory hydration; bootstrap rows bypass process_user_order, database status writes, fill accounting, and follow-up creation.

Every complete Coinbase envelope's canonical live PATCH/UPDATE rows are atomically admitted to bounded FIFO lanes keyed by client_order_id, then run one process_user_order path for hooks, normalization, stealth exchange-ID sync, memory update, narrow parent/progress locking, persistence, status routing, dashboard publication, and terminal eviction. EXPIRED performs cleanup without filled/cancelled replacement handlers.

Position members are generation-fenced and rejected after desynchronization, then processed independently before order reduction; shape or hook failure is logged without suppressing valid order work or changing the order bootstrap phase for a positions-only event.

Configured public channels use redundant WSClient-owned wrappers; user/futures-balance plus heartbeat use exactly one WSUserClient wrapper and an engine-owned reconnect generation. Every worker checks stop, subscribes only to its role channels, polls the SDK, and disconnects in finally after a connection attempt.

Public JSON uses EventBridge payload dedup and ticker-specific overflow recovery. Private JSON bypasses payload hashing, validates configured channels and complete envelopes against one connection-global sequence, retains generation/timestamp/channel, ignores only exact sequence replays, and desynchronizes plus reconnects on conflicts, gaps, malformed input, or bounded-queue overflow.
